description:
Two independently reproduced compiler defects allow a plain map to reach code
that asserts a named struct. They share the required semantic invariant—plain
maps must not satisfy named-struct dispatch—but they do not currently share the
mechanism described by the old ticket.

## 1. Source `%Struct{}` patterns emit no struct discriminator

    defmodule Box do
      defstruct [:value]
    end

    fn classify(v) do
      case v do
        %Box{value: x} -> {:box, x}
        _ -> :other
      end
    end

    fn main() do
      dbg(classify(%Box{value: 7}))
      dbg(classify(%{1 => :one}))
    end

At origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83:

    $ ./target/debug/fz2 interp /tmp/fz-kdt27-box.fz
    {:box, 7}
    fz2 interp: backend executable 3 function 31 entry 1 step evaluation failed:
      match_error: expected struct Box

`run` prints `{:box, 7}` and halts through a match-error fault trap. `build`
succeeds, and its binary does the same.

The backend dump for `classify/1[%{1 => :one}]` has `graph root=n1` with `n1
outcome o0`; there is no runtime type or map-shape test. The chosen entry then
executes `assert_struct v0 %Box`.

This follows directly from `src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs:647-650`:
`Pattern::Struct` ignores `module` and recursively applies every field pattern
to the original struct subject. For `%Box{value: x}`, the variable produces no
question, making the struct row irrefutable. Non-variable field patterns are
also aimed at the whole subject rather than a field projection.

## 2. Mixed named-struct/map protocol receivers lose the Map arm

    fn counted(value), do: Enumerable.count(value)

    fn main() do
      values = [Range.new(1, 9, 2), %{1 => :one, 2 => :two}]
      result = case values do
        [r, map] -> {counted(r), counted(map)}
        _ -> :bad_shape
      end
      dbg(result)
    end

Current result:

    interp:
      match_error: expected struct Range
    run:
      match_error: the root process halted through a fault trap
    AOT:
      match_error: the main process halted through a fault trap

The backend dump contains one `counted/1` activation whose receiver includes
both the Range struct evidence and the plain map. Its call is direct to
`Enumerable.Range.count/1`; that executable immediately asserts `%Range`, so
the second invocation fails.

Protocol matching uses `protocol_receiver_target_overlaps`
(`src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:1481-1487`). Its runtime projection sets:

    named_structs: named_structs.clone()
    maps: !descr.maps.is_empty() && named_structs.is_none()

(`src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:1342-1344`).

`World::struct_value_ty` represents a struct using nominal, tuple, and map
evidence (`src/compiler2/world.rs:1916-1932`). Once a real `Range` and a plain
map are joined, the receiver has a named struct and map clauses. The global
`named_structs.is_none()` gate suppresses the entire map axis, including the
independent plain-map alternative. Map therefore fails to become a viable
protocol target.

The same mechanism explains the deferred three-way fixture. Direct execution of
`fixtures2/behavior/enumerable_protocol_dispatch.fz` currently gives:

    interp:
      backend dispatch callsite in executable 8 missed an exhaustive dispatch
    run/AOT:
      compiler2_unreachable_control ... halted through a fault trap

Its backend call edge has only Range and List arms with `miss=Unreachable`;
there is no Map arm. The runtime map misses both supposedly exhaustive arms.

The existing unit test
`runtime_type_predicate_keeps_named_struct_identity_out_of_plain_map_kind`
passes, but covers a Range alone. The missing case is a union containing both a
named struct and an independent plain map.

## Required checks

- The `%Box{}`/wildcard repro prints `{:box, 7}` then `:other` on interp, run,
  and AOT.
- A source-plan or backend assertion proves `%Box{...}` contains a named-struct
  discriminator; field subpatterns are projected to their named fields rather
  than tested against the whole struct.
- `Enumerable.count` over `Range | Map` returns
  `{{:ok, 5}, {:ok, 2}}` on all three paths.
- A runtime-predicate unit test proves `Range | Map` retains both the Range
  named-struct axis and the independent Map axis while Range alone still does
  not match Map.
- The three defer lines are removed from
  `fixtures2/behavior/enumerable_protocol_dispatch.fz`, and all three matrix
  lanes pass with `{{:ok, 3}, {:ok, 5}, {:ok, 2}}`.
- `membership_operator` remains green on all three lanes.
- Full library and fixture matrix pass.
title: Plain maps reach struct bodies through two nominal-identity losses: %Struct{} emits no struct question and Struct | Map protocol unions drop Map
